raw_case_text: A 35-year-old male patient presented with multiple asymptomatic erythematous raised lesions over the face, neck, trunk, and both upper limbs for the last 2 months. He had a history of intermittent low-grade fever for the last 3 months without chills and rigors. A history of swelling of the face for the last 20 days was present. It first appeared on the neck, hand, and nose, and later it progressed to involve the trunk, both upper limbs, and the entire face. No plaques were found in the penis and lower limb. He had a history of unprotected sexual intercourse with both male and female partners. There was no history of blood transfusion or intravenous drug abuse. Systemic symptoms present were nausea, vomiting, and fever. On examination, (after the patient has given informed consent), the patient had generalized lymphadenopathy without hepatosplenomegaly. Cutaneous examination revealed multiple, discrete, violaceous plaques measuring 0.5 cm x 0.5 cm to 3 cm x 2 cm over the trunk, face [Figure 1, left one], neck, and both upper extremities [Figure 2]. On oral examination, there were erythematous plaques over the left tonsillar fossa and posterior pharyngeal wall [Figure 3]. He had low hemoglobin (8.4 g/dL), low platelets (38,000/mm3), and normal liver and renal function; serology for HIV-1 was positive by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and negative for HIV-2, and his CD4 count was 337/mm3. Hepatitis B surface antigen was reactive. Ultrasonography of the whole abdomen showed a space-occupying lesion in segment 7 of the liver suggestive of hemangioma. Histopathological examination showed irregularly distributed vascular channels, some of which were surrounding preexisting vessels, with jagged outline throughout the dermis and were lined by a single layer of endothelial cells, cords, and clumps of spindle cells between dermal collagen bundles, with cells having plump vesicular nuclei [Figure 4]. Patchy lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates were seen in the dermis around the blood vessels and adnexal structures and beneath the epidermis. Immunostaining was performed for CD34. Endothelial cells and spindle cells were strongly immunoreactive. A contrast-enhanced computed tomography scan of the thorax was performed, which showed patchy air space opacities in both lung fields and a well-defined hypodense lesion in the liver, suggestive of KS. A final diagnosis of HIV-associated Kaposi sarcoma (plaque stage) was made. The patient was on antiretroviral therapy (ART) (tenofovir, lamivudine, and efavirenz regimen) and had received ten cycles of EBRT for facial lesions and developed erosions over the lips and tongues. The patient's facial lesions had resolved with hyperpigmentation including oral lesions, but lesions over the trunk and limbs were present [Figure 1 right one]. The patient had received pegylated liposomal doxorubicin in six cycles.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 35-year-old male presented with a 3-month history of intermittent low-grade fever, a 2-month history of multiple asymptomatic erythematous-to-violaceous raised plaques over his face, neck, trunk, and upper limbs, and a 20-day history of facial swelling.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed intermittent low-grade fevers without chills 3 months prior to presentation, followed 2 months prior by asymptomatic violaceous plaques starting on the neck, hand, and nose and spreading across the face, trunk, and bilateral upper extremities, and 20 days of progressive facial edema accompanied by nausea and vomiting.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unremarkable prior medical history; sexual history notable for unprotected sexual intercourse with both male and female partners; denied blood transfusions or intravenous drug use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 3-month intermittent low-grade fever, nausea, vomiting, facial swelling, and widespread painless violaceous skin and oral plaques; negative for chills, rigors, or penile/lower-limb skin lesions.

objective.physical_examination: Generalized peripheral lymphadenopathy without hepatosplenomegaly, accompanied by facial edema. Cutaneous examination revealed multiple discrete violaceous plaques (measuring 0.5 x 0.5 cm to 3 x 2 cm) over the face, neck, trunk, and bilateral upper extremities (sparing the penis and lower extremities). Intraoral examination revealed erythematous-violaceous plaques over the left tonsillar fossa and posterior pharyngeal wall.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs showed anemia (hemoglobin 8.4 g/dL), severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 38,000/mm3), normal liver and renal function tests, reactive HBsAg, and positive HIV-1 ELISA (negative for HIV-2). Abdominal ultrasonography showed a hypodense lesion in hepatic segment VII.
objective.advanced_workup: Baseline CD4+ T-cell count was 337 cells/mm3. Contrast-enhanced chest and upper abdominal CT demonstrated bilateral patchy pulmonary airspace opacities and a well-defined hypodense hepatic lesion suggestive of visceral Kaposi sarcoma. Skin biopsy histopathology and immunohistochemistry demonstrated jagged dermal vascular channels surrounding pre-existing vessels ('promontory sign'), cords of spindle cells with plump vesicular nuclei between collagen bundles, perivascular lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates, and strong CD34 immunoreactivity in endothelial and spindle cells.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Disseminated plaque-stage mucocutaneous, nodal, pulmonary, and hepatic Kaposi sarcoma unmasking newly diagnosed HIV-1 and chronic hepatitis B virus (HBsAg+) co-infection (CD4+ count 337 cells/mm3; confirmed by skin biopsy histopathology, CD34+ immunohistochemistry, and thoracoabdominal CT). Treated with combination antiretroviral therapy (tenofovir, lamivudine, and efavirenz), 10 fractions of external-beam radiotherapy (EBRT) to the facial lesions (complicated by transient lip and lingual radiation mucositis, achieving complete resolution of facial and oral lesions with residual hyperpigmentation), and 6 cycles of systemic pegylated liposomal doxorubicin.
